---
title: "Troubleshooting"
execute:
  eval: false
---

Diagnose from the outside inward: TLS/Apache, LDAP, loopback Shiny, application
logs, database, then external mail/storage. Do not make the system reachable by
disabling certificate checks, exposing port 3838, switching production to test
auth, accepting a client identity header, or making files world-writable.

## First-response snapshot

```bash
sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status apache2 shiny-server.service \
  ppsv-mail-outbox.timer ppsv-backup.timer
sudo journalctl -u apache2 -u shiny-server.service --since '-30 minutes'
sudo apache2ctl configtest
sudo ss -ltnp | grep 3838
sudo readlink -f /srv/shiny-server/ppsvf-app
sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /etc/ppsvf-app/ppsvf-app.env \
  /srv/ppsvf-app-data/ppsv_projects.db
```

Do not print the entire environment file into a ticket or shared terminal log;
it contains SMTP credentials.

## HTTPS or redirect failure

Check both public routes without `-k`:

```bash
curl -I http://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/
curl -I https://ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/
sudo apache2ctl configtest
sudo tail -n 100 /var/log/apache2/ppsvf-app-ssl-error.log
```

Expected: HTTP redirects to HTTPS, and HTTPS `/` redirects to `/ppsvf-app/`
after normal CA validation. If validation fails, inspect the leaf SAN, expiry,
bundle order, intermediate chain, and key match. Rerun provisioning with the
correct TLS source files; do not copy a guessed key or a CSR into place.

## `/ppsvf-app/` returns 404 or 502

```bash
sudo readlink -f /srv/shiny-server/ppsvf-app
sudo test -f /srv/shiny-server/ppsvf-app/app.R
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3838/ppsvf-app/
sudo journalctl -u shiny-server.service -n 150 --no-pager
sudo find /var/log/shiny-server -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*ppsv*' -print
```

A 404 normally means the active symlink/release or proxy path is wrong. A 502
normally means Shiny is down or not listening. Confirm the active release has
`app.R`, `renv.lock`, and its restored library, then use the deployment or
rollback script. Do not copy mutable state into the release to make it start.

## LDAP prompt succeeds but the application has no identity

Confirm only non-secret settings and the active vhost:

```bash
sudo grep -E '^(AUTH_MODE|PPSV_PUBLIC_URL)=' /etc/ppsvf-app/ppsvf-app.env
sudo apache2ctl -M | grep -E 'authnz_ldap|headers|proxy|proxy_wstunnel'
sudo grep -n 'RequestHeader.*X-Remote' \
  /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ppsv-vm-shiny-443.conf
sudo tail -n 100 /var/log/apache2/ppsvf-app-ssl-error.log
```

`AUTH_MODE` must be `ldap`. Apache must remove client identity headers at
virtual-host scope and set authenticated values inside the protected location.
Do not add an identity query string, cookie, app-local login, default password,
or `.Renviron` workaround.

If an LDAP attribute is legitimately absent, name/email may be entered manually
and remain unverified. That is different from a missing authenticated username,
which must fail closed.

## A user has the wrong role or cannot sign in

Normalize the username to lowercase and compare it with the fixed allowlist in
`ppsvf-app/R/config.R`. Roles cannot be edited in the admin directory and do not
come from `b_profa`. Check the account's active flag and last login in the admin
directory.

If the account is inactive, an administrator may reactivate the non-admin user.
If the allowlist is wrong, make a reviewed code change with authorization tests
and deploy a new release; do not edit a database role.

## Database startup or migration error

```bash
sudo -u ppsvf-shiny-user sqlite3 /srv/ppsvf-app-data/ppsv_projects.db \
  'PRAGMA integrity_check; SELECT * FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;'
sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /srv/ppsvf-app-data/ppsv_projects.db*
sudo journalctl -u shiny-server.service -n 150 --no-pager
```

Integrity must be `ok`; database, WAL, and SHM files must remain private to the
service identity/group. A deployment initializes the database only when absent
and applies later migrations transactionally. Do not point PPSV at
`ms_projects.db`, use a reset flag, or delete the database as a repair.

For integrity failure, stop writers, preserve evidence, verify the newest
external backup, and follow [Backup and restore](backup-restore.qmd). For a code
compatibility problem, roll back code first; remember that migrations remain.

## Ticket delivery is pending, retrying, or failed

```bash
sudo systemctl start ppsv-mail-outbox.service
sudo systemctl status ppsv-mail-outbox.service --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u ppsv-mail-outbox.service -n 150 --no-pager
```

In the staff delivery log, inspect sender, recipient, reply-to, mode, attempt
count, next attempt, and last error.

- `disabled` or a suppressed configuration-error row means the request was
  saved but delivery was intentionally not attempted.
- Authentication or relay errors require SMTP-owner review; do not substitute
  the editable form email.
- An LDAP-`From` rejection should activate the fixed service-sender fallback
  immediately.
- Fixed-sender failures retry at the documented schedule and remain durable.
- Only an admin can reset a failed row for manual retry.

Before retrying, determine whether the ticket or acknowledgement actually
arrived despite an ambiguous timeout. A duplicate ticket is worse than leaving
the row failed while the incident is investigated.

If the requester got two acknowledgements, repeat the real ticket behavior test
and correct `PPSV_DIRECT_ACK`; do not alter stored delivery rows to hide it.

## Upload fell back to local storage

Confirm the mount identity, permissions, and service-user access:

```bash
findmnt -T /fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
sudo getfacl /fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
sudo -u ppsvf-shiny-user test -w /fs/pool/pool-ppsvf-projects
sudo find /srv/ppsvf-app-data/uploads_pending_pool -maxdepth 3 -type f -print
```

Do not recursively `chmod 777`, `chmod 666`, or `chown` the facility pool. Ask
the storage owner to restore the mount/ACL. When it is writable, run:

```bash
sudo systemctl start ppsv-pool-reconcile.service
sudo journalctl -u ppsv-pool-reconcile.service -n 150 --no-pager
```

Reconciliation deliberately leaves source copies. Investigate checksum or
destination conflicts individually instead of overwriting them.

If neither pool nor fallback is writable, submissions containing files are
correctly rejected. Repair storage; never accept a record that silently loses
an upload.

## File download reports missing, unsafe, or checksum failure

Do not bypass the authorized download handler. Compare the database manifest
with the configured root, check for a changed mount, symlink, moved file, or
checksum mismatch, and preserve the suspect file. Restore from the matching
pool snapshot/fallback backup only after identifying the correct recovery
point.

An archived file remains stored but is omitted from the normal manifest. Only
an administrator can archive it.

## Backup job failed

```bash
sudo systemctl status ppsv-backup.service --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u ppsv-backup.service -n 150 --no-pager
sudo grep '^PPSV_BACKUP_DIR=' /etc/ppsvf-app/ppsvf-app.env
findmnt -T /the/configured/backup/path
df -h /the/configured/backup/path
```

Common causes are a missing external mount, no free space, permissions, a held
operation lock, or SQLite integrity failure. Confirm the path is the intended
external filesystem, not an accidentally created directory on `/`. Fix the
cause and start the service again; then verify new artifacts and sidecars and
run the read-only restore check.

## PDF rendering problem

Confirm the locked R environment was restored and that font/image system
libraries passed `scripts/check_requirements.sh`. Reproduce with a representative
Unicode/multiline request. PDF failure must not modify request state. Do not add
cost, invoice, or legacy templates as a workaround.

## Deployment failed after migration

The deploy script restores the previous code symlink if the new release fails
its loopback health check, but a committed database migration remains. Read the
deployment error and Shiny log, then choose a release compatible with the
current schema. Use database restore only with incident authorization and the
explicit data-loss confirmation described in [Backup and restore](backup-restore.qmd).

## Escalation bundle

Provide the incident owner with timestamps, release ID/revision, affected
request code (not secret form content), relevant unit status/log excerpts,
outbox error text, database integrity result, mount identity, and steps already
tried. Redact SMTP password, LDAP credentials, TLS private key, form sequences,
and other sensitive request data.
